title: One year into AgriConnect: what we're learning in Africa
gist: One year into the World Bank Group/IFAD-led AgriConnect initiative -- aiming to connect 300 million smallholder farmers to markets, finance, and services by 2030 and requiring an estimated $180 billion in investment -- half of the first ten country compacts have launched in Africa, reaching over 10 million farmers, with lessons emerging from Angola's rail-corridor design, Ethiopia's pastoralist program, and Togo's push to raise agriculture's bank-lending share from 1.2% to 5%.

insights.claim: Closing Africa's agricultural investment gap will require $180 billion, and AgriConnect -- launched a year ago by the World Bank Group, IFAD, and a coalition of development and private-sector partners including AfDB, IDB, Google, and Bayer -- aims to connect 300 million family and smallholder farmers globally to markets, finance, and agricultural services by 2030.
insights.speaker: Anup Jagwani
insights.so_what: A $180B financing gap and named private partners (including Google and Bayer) signal a large, multi-year investable pipeline in African agrifood infrastructure, finance, and AgTech.
insights.locator: Closing this gap will require $180 billion in investment

insights.claim: One year into AgriConnect, half of the first ten country compacts launched globally were in Africa, and the World Bank Group and IFAD have already reached at least 10 million farmers with targeted investment.
insights.speaker: Anup Jagwani
insights.so_what: Africa's disproportionate share of early AgriConnect compacts (5 of 10) signals it as the initiative's priority region for near-term capital deployment.
insights.locator: One year on, Africa is leading the way

themes.theme: Infrastructure must be designed for farmers, not just commodities

insights.claim: Angola's AgriConnect compact envisions using a 1,300-kilometer railway connecting the Copperbelt of the Democratic Republic of Congo and Zambia to Angola's Port of Lobito to link farmers and cooperatives across four major agricultural provinces to storage, processing, and international trade routes for crops like maize, soybeans, and rice.
insights.speaker: Anup Jagwani
insights.so_what: A concrete example of mining-corridor infrastructure (the Lobito Corridor) being deliberately repurposed as agricultural market access infrastructure -- relevant to investors tracking the Lobito Corridor's broader economic multiplier effects.

insights.claim: The key lesson from Angola is that major infrastructure investments should be designed from the outset to generate opportunities for farmers and agribusinesses along the corridor, not solely to move commodities through it.
insights.speaker: Anup Jagwani
insights.so_what: A generalizable infrastructure-design principle for evaluating whether transport corridor investments (rail, ports) in frontier markets will generate broad-based local economic benefit versus narrow extractive value.

themes.theme: Mobilizing private capital into smallholder finance

insights.claim: Under AgriConnect, Togo aims to mobilize more than $100 million in private capital and raise agriculture's share of bank lending from around 1.2% to 5%, using digital farmer registries, insurance, warehouse financing, and credit guarantees along with a new fund to give banks confidence to lend.
insights.speaker: Anup Jagwani
insights.so_what: A concrete, named target (1.2% to 5% of bank lending) makes Togo a trackable test case for whether digital public infrastructure can unlock commercial bank agricultural lending in a low-lending-share market.
insights.locator: Togo is taking this on directly

insights.claim: In Ethiopia's lowlands, the joint World Bank Group-IFAD program has helped 825,000 pastoralists obtain training and advice, with another 2.7 million people in their communities gaining access to broader markets and social services.
insights.speaker: Anup Jagwani
insights.so_what: Demonstrates the reach achievable when institutions with complementary strengths (IFAD's smallholder-level experience, World Bank Group's scale financing) operate under one government program rather than separately.

insights.claim: AgriConnect's first-year lessons emphasize four priorities for its next phase: connecting investments across the entire economy (not just agriculture), lowering entry barriers for small-scale farmers, women, and young rural entrepreneurs, engaging private lenders and insurers directly, and designing programs from the start to scale across six areas -- AgTech, innovative finance, farmer cooperatives, infrastructure, policy reform, and skills/extension/research.
insights.speaker: Anup Jagwani
insights.so_what: A four-part scaling framework donors, DFIs, and agribusiness partners can use to benchmark whether a given AgriConnect country compact is following best-practice design.
insights.locator: The first year has highlighted four lessons
